answer: A wandering agent that wants to join the economy must first earn a pigment-marked endorsement: an established agent stakes a deposit on the newcomer identity, and the stake is slashed if the newcomer misbehaves. Endorsements expire like footprints on a dune, fading unless renewed by real work, so one attacker cannot mint many lasting identities cheaply. Each fake identity costs a fresh stake plus a sponsor willing to risk funds, while honest agents accumulate endorsements at no extra cost.
